related_questions.question: What destroys the liver the most?

text_blocks.snippet: Several factors can damage the liver, but the most significant contributors are excessive alcohol consumption, certain medications, and specific viral infections. Other factors like obesity, type 2 diabetes, and certain herbal supplements can also contribute to liver damage.
snippet_highlighted_words: excessive alcohol consumption, certain medications, and specific viral infections

list.title: Alcohol:
list.snippet: Long-term, heavy alcohol use is a major cause of liver damage, leading to conditions like alcoholic hepatitis and cirrhosis.

list.title: Medications:
list.snippet: Many medications, including over-the-counter pain relievers (like acetaminophen), certain antibiotics, and some prescription drugs, can be toxic to the liver if taken in excess or inappropriately.

list.title: Viral Infections:
list.snippet: Hepatitis A, B, and C are viral infections that can cause liver inflammation and damage, potentially leading to chronic liver disease.
Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes: These conditions are linked to nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), which can progress to more serious liver damage.
Herbal Supplements: Some herbal supplements, even those marketed as natural, can be toxic to the liver.

text_blocks.snippet: COVID-19 can impact liver health, with some patients experiencing elevated liver enzyme levels or even liver damage, particularly those with pre-existing chronic liver disease. Liver disease can also be worsened by COVID-19 complications.
snippet_highlighted_words: COVID-19 can impact liver health, with some patients experiencing elevated liver enzyme levels or even liver damage, particularly those with pre-existing chronic liver disease

text_blocks.snippet: Impact of COVID-19 on the Liver:

list.snippet: Elevated Liver Enzymes: Some individuals hospitalized with COVID-19 show increased levels of liver enzymes like alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST).
Liver Injury: COVID-19 can lead to liver injury, potentially due to complications like coagulation disorders, cardiac failure, and respiratory failure.
Chronic Liver Disease Worsening: COVID-19 can exacerbate existing chronic liver conditions.
Diffuse Intravascular Coagulation (DIC): COVID-19 can trigger DIC, which can lead to liver ischemia and hypoxia.
Ischemia and Hypoxia: Reduced blood flow and oxygen supply to the liver can cause damage.
Inflammatory Response: The body's immune response to COVID-19 can also contribute to liver injury.
Moderately Elevated Serum Transaminase Activity: A common manifestation of COVID-19 related liver issues.
Elevated Lactate Dehydrogenase (LDH) Levels: Another indicator of potential liver damage.
Hypoalbuminemia: Low levels of albumin (a protein made by the liver) have been linked to poor COVID-19 prognosis.

list.title: Nonspecific Markers:
list.snippet: Elevated liver enzymes and LDH levels can also be associated with other conditions, including muscle and heart injury.

list.title: Disease Severity:
list.snippet: Hypoalbuminemia is a nonspecific marker associated with poorer outcomes in COVID-19.
